claims.text: Nearly equiatomic five-transition-metal HEA nanoparticles have intrinsic thermal stability and resistance to atomic diffusion that are compromised by nanoparticle surface effects.
Surface-induced lattice relaxation causes phase separation or amorphization at lower temperatures than bulk configurational-entropy models predict.
A critical particle size exists below which surface-to-volume effects dominate bulk entropy contributions.
The proposed initial nanoparticles are single-phase solid solutions with high configurational entropy and severe lattice distortion.
The nanoparticle surface has reduced local atomic coordination and permits relaxation of severe lattice distortion.
Surface relaxation lowers the activation-energy barrier for atomic diffusion.
The reduced diffusion barrier destabilizes the single-phase solid solution.
High configurational entropy can reduce the thermodynamic driving force for precipitation and stabilize a single-phase HEA solid solution.
Severe lattice distortion in NbTaTiV impedes dislocation motion.
High nanoparticle surface energy reduces the effective configurational-entropy contribution to stability.
Surface relaxation facilitates faster atomic diffusion and nucleation of secondary phases or amorphization.
Bulk thermodynamic models do not capture the proposed nanoparticle surface-relaxation mechanism.
Nanoparticles smaller than 20 nm will phase-separate or amorphize 200–300°C below the corresponding bulk material.
Nanoparticles smaller than 20 nm will have diffusion coefficients significantly higher than predicted by the sluggish-diffusion hypothesis.
Bulk NbTaTiV remains a stable single-phase material with sluggish diffusion up to 900°C.
A robust surface oxide shell can stabilize the nanoparticles against the proposed surface-driven evolution.
For particle sizes above 100 nm, surface effects become negligible relative to bulk entropy and behavior becomes bulk-like.
The cited evidence is limited to bulk or coating systems rather than five-component HEA nanoparticles.

contradictions.description: The target is repeatedly described as a five-transition-metal alloy, but NbTaTiV, the principal example and baseline, contains only four elements.
